# Notable liberties

30 places where the kit departs from, reinterprets, or extends Apple's Human Interface Guidelines for the web.
The Standards column lists the catalog entries in [STANDARDS.md](STANDARDS.md) that cite each liberty.

| ID | Liberty | Why | Standards |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LIB-01** | **pt → px 1:1, then rem.** A HIG point equals one CSS px at the device's scale factor. Evidence: Playwright 1.64.1 describes iPhone 17 Pro as 402 px wide @3× DPR, and Apple publishes 402 pt wide for that phone (⚠ the live HIG no longer lists device specs, so the pt figure comes from memory and is unverified). Sizes are then written in rem at a 16 px root. The CSS `pt` unit (1/72 in = 1.333 px) is **banned**, because it would turn 17 pt into 22.7 px. | Correct, testable translation. Stylelint `unit-disallowed-list: ["pt"]`. | — |
| **LIB-02** | **Dynamic Type → rem plus browser text size and zoom.** No web API exposes the iOS Dynamic Type category. Optional: WebKit's `font: -apple-system-body` on `html` reportedly tracks Dynamic Type in Safari, then the family is reset. ⚠ Not verified this pass; test on a device before adopting. | The nearest web mechanism. | — |
| **LIB-03** | **One type scale (iOS "Large" defaults) for all widths.** The macOS 13 pt body is too small for web reading. Two display sizes above Large Title are added for storefront heroes, using fluid `clamp()` with rem bounds and covered by the 200% zoom tests. | Storefront marketing needs bigger headings than HIG apps. | — |
| **LIB-04** | **WCAG's definition of large text replaces HIG's table.** HIG's contrast table gives 3:1 for bold text at any size and for 18 pt and up. WCAG's "large text" is ≥ 18 pt (24 px) regular or ≥ 14 pt (18.66 px) bold. So small bold text still needs 4.5:1. HIG's dark-mode "strive for 7:1" is adopted for primary and secondary text. | HIG's table is looser than the WCAG text it cites; WCAG is the legal and audit standard. | [COL-01](STANDARDS.md#color-col) |
| **LIB-05** | **Targets: 44 px by default; HIG's 28 pt "minimum" is not used.** WCAG's 24 px floor applies only to dense inline cases. | HIG's 28 pt minimum is below the comfortable touch size; 44 also equals WCAG 2.5.5 AAA. | — |
| **LIB-06** | **Accessibility settings → media queries.** Increase Contrast → `prefers-contrast: more` (Chrome 96 / Safari 14.1 / Firefox 101). Reduce Transparency → `prefers-reduced-transparency` (Chrome 118; **not** Safari; Firefox behind a flag), so opaque fallbacks also key off `prefers-contrast`. Bold Text has **no web equivalent** and is dropped. Windows `forced-colors` is added. | Browser support per BCD 8.1.8. | — |
| **LIB-07** | **Liquid Glass → `backdrop-filter` material** (blur + saturate over a role-tinted surface at a fixed opacity floor), with opaque fallbacks. No lensing, refraction, or specular highlights. `-webkit-backdrop-filter` is still emitted (BCD: unprefixed Safari 18; Chrome 76; Firefox 103). | Cheap, legible, and avoids imitating Apple trade dress (§3.1). | — |
| **LIB-08** | **Safe areas → `env(safe-area-inset-*)`** with `viewport-fit=cover` (Chrome 69 / Safari 11.1 / Firefox 65). Dynamic Island and camera housing are covered by the same insets. | Direct web equivalent. | — |
| **LIB-09** | **Size classes → width breakpoints plus container queries** (Chrome 105 / Safari 16 / Firefox 110). The vertical size class is approximated by a `max-height` query only for landscape phones. | The web has no size-class API. | — |
| **LIB-10** | **System colors → our own palette** under HIG-style semantic role names. Apple's measured values are not reused (system blue light is 3.52:1 on white). Our tertiary label meets 4.5:1, unlike HIG's low-alpha tertiary/quaternary; quaternary is reserved for disabled UI. | Accessibility and independence from Apple's values. | — |
| **LIB-11** | **SF Symbols → Lucide** (ISC + MIT). A stroke-width token stands in for symbol weights, and icons size in `em`. | License (§3.1). | — |
| **LIB-12** | **One open font set everywhere; no San Francisco.** Inter for UI and body text, Source Serif 4 for optional editorial headings, IBM Plex Mono for code and numbers. All are OFL-1.1 and in Shopify's font library. System-font keywords that would render SF Pro on Apple devices are not used either. | Owner decision (2026-11-03): zero licensing ambiguity (§3.1), and the same rendering on every platform, which keeps visual baselines deterministic. | [TYP-12](STANDARDS.md#typography-typ) |
| **LIB-13** | **Haptics and audio cues dropped.** Feedback is visual plus a live region. Copy says "select", not "tap"/"click". | ⚠ Web Vibration support on iOS Safari not verified; HIG haptic patterns don't apply. | [WRT-06](STANDARDS.md#writing-wrt) |
| **LIB-14** | **Platform-only guidance dropped:** menu bar, Dock, windows/panels, widgets, Live Activities, complications, Digital Crown, Apple Pencil, Action button, Camera Control, tvOS focus engine and safe-area figures, visionOS spatial/ornaments, game controls, Siri/Shortcuts, App Clips, app icons (favicon/touch icon only), Spotlight, Quick Look. | Not applicable to responsive web storefronts. | — |
| **LIB-15** | **Optional site appearance toggle,** defaulting to System. HIG advises against app-specific appearance settings. | Some merchants require a brand-fixed theme. Allowed only when it defaults to System. | [DRK-01](STANDARDS.md#dark-mode-drk) |
| **LIB-16** | **Submit stays enabled.** HIG suggests enabling Next only once required data is present. Disabled buttons are not focusable and give no reason, so the kit validates on submit and focuses the first error. | Web a11y practice (WCAG 3.3.1/3.3.3). | [FRM-08](STANDARDS.md#forms-and-inputs-frm) |
| **LIB-17** | **Sentence case everywhere.** HIG's Alerts page says button titles take sentence-style capitalisation, but Menus says menu items take title-style. The kit unifies on sentence case. | Consistency, as HIG Writing itself requires. | [WRT-03](STANDARDS.md#writing-wrt) |
| **LIB-18** | **All controls are Tab-focusable.** HIG's iPadOS keyboard note discourages keyboard navigation on buttons and switches, leaving that to Full Keyboard Access. | On the web, WCAG 2.1.1 requires it. | — |
| **LIB-19** | **Dialog button order uses logical flex order,** so it mirrors in RTL. | HIG gives physical (trailing) placement. | — |
| **LIB-20** | **Tab bar → header navigation plus an optional compact bottom bar (≤ 5 items, ours).** HIG's floating Liquid Glass tab bar is not replicated. | Storefront convention. The live Tab bars page gives no numeric limit, so 5 is ours. | [NAV-02](STANDARDS.md#navigation-and-search-nav) |
| **LIB-21** | **Sheet detents → CSS bottom sheets** with 50% / 90% `dvh` snap points via scroll-snap, plus a grabber. | Nearest web pattern. | — |
| **LIB-22** | **Elevated dark surfaces are explicit tokens** applied by components, not automatic. | The web has no automatic elevated trait. | — |
| **LIB-23** | **Motion numbers are ours.** HIG gives no durations; tokens are capped at 400 ms. | Needed for automated checks. | — |
| **LIB-24** | **Readable width is ours:** 66ch target / 75ch max. HIG mentions readable-width guides but gives no number. | Needed for automated checks. | — |
| **LIB-25** | **Web and commerce extensions not in HIG:** skip link, breadcrumbs, cookie/age-consent banners (legal, so exempt from MOD-09), performance budgets, Shopify Theme Store floors. | Web requirements. | [NAV-09](STANDARDS.md#navigation-and-search-nav), [NAV-13](STANDARDS.md#navigation-and-search-nav), [MOD-09](STANDARDS.md#modals-sheets-popovers-alerts-mod), [COM-07](STANDARDS.md#commerce-patterns-com) |
| **LIB-26** | **Apple Pay rules constrain only our layout.** Shopify's dynamic checkout renders the actual buttons. | We don't control those buttons. | — |
| **LIB-27** | **Clay vocabulary, adapted:** Clay's physical `LEFT`/`RIGHT` become logical `start`/`end` on the web. Clay's `PERCENT` subtracts padding *and* gaps; CSS % does not, so the web shim uses `calc()`. Clay has no wrap or grid, so `Cluster` and `Grid` are web-only primitives (§4.5). | Fidelity where natural, per the captain's intent. | — |
| **LIB-28** | **HIG spacing advice (~12/24 pt) is a warning, not an error.** | It is approximate in HIG itself. | — |
| **LIB-29** | **Shopify Theme Store floors adopted** (Lighthouse perf ≥ 60, a11y ≥ 90 average; contrast; 24 px targets), with stricter kit targets on top. | Client themes may later be listed. | — |
| **LIB-30** | **Haptic "press" feel → a pressed visual state** (scale ≤ 0.98 or a fill change), disabled under reduced motion. | Web substitute. | — |

Notes:

- **LIB-12**: Revised from the research report, which proposed SF Pro through system-font keywords with an Inter fallback.
